questions.q: A job has been sitting in the Preparing status for several minutes on its first run. What is most likely happening?
options: Your model is overfitting
The compute cluster has run out of quota
The environment (Docker image or conda setup) is being built
The job has already failed
questions.explain: Preparing means the run environment is being set up: a Docker image build or a conda environment. The first run can be slow; later runs can reuse what was built.

questions.q: Why should a training script write its model and metrics files to a named output or the outputs folder?
options: The compute is temporary, so files on its own disk are lost unless they land where the job keeps them
Because Python cannot write to other folders on cloud compute
Because outputs make the job run faster
Because the studio cannot display print statements otherwise
questions.explain: Compute is created for the job and released afterward. Results must be saved to a job output so you can retrieve them later.

questions.q: In a command job, how do you refer to a named output called model_dir inside the command string?
options: ${{inputs.model_dir}}
%model_dir%
${{outputs.model_dir}}
outputs["model_dir"]
questions.explain: Inputs use ${{inputs.<name>}} and outputs use ${{outputs.<name>}}. An output left with default settings is a uri_folder, and Azure ML generates its location.

questions.q: A job ends as Failed. Where should you look first for your script's traceback?
options: The system_logs folder, because it holds your print output
std_log.txt in the user_logs folder of the Outputs + logs tab
The Key Vault audit log
The compute instance's notebook history
questions.explain: std_log.txt contains the stdout and stderr of your script, so prints and tracebacks appear there. system_logs holds messages generated by Azure ML itself.

questions.q: What does limits.timeout in a command job's YAML do?
options: It sets how long the environment image is cached
It limits the number of training rows
It sets how long the studio page stays open
It sets the maximum number of seconds the job may run before the system cancels it
questions.explain: The YAML schema describes limits.timeout as the maximum time in seconds the job is allowed to run; when reached, the system cancels it. It protects you from runaway compute cost.
